sources.title: Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Annual Report 2024–25
sources.period: Report FY 2024–25; APY 2021–22 to 2023–24; horticulture 2023–24 third advance estimates

sources.title: Drip and sprinkler irrigation through PMKSY — Lok Sabha Q2767
sources.publisher: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare / Lok Sabha
sources.period: Cumulative FY 2015–16 to March 2025; scheme governance since FY 2022–23
claims: PDMC moved from PMKSY to PM-RKVY from FY 2022–23.

findings.title: Haryana transport-lifting penalties assessed but not imposed
findings.finding: CAG calculated ₹54.90 crore leviable transport penalties and reported no penalty imposed for delayed lifting.

amount.status: Audit-assessed levy; not recovered cash or proven theft

findings.response: The Department said COVID-19 restrictions made procurement difficult and penalising transporters during the pandemic was inappropriate. CAG said no State Government penalty-waiver decision existed.
alternativeExplanations: Pandemic transport disruption and continuity-of-procurement priorities, as raised by the Department.
Audited 2020 data covered only 14,159 vehicles because complete data was unavailable.
Liability requires contract-by-contract attribution of delay; audit estimate should not be treated as every contract's adjudicated debt.
findings.falsifier: An authorized waiver, reconciled vehicle-level logs showing non-contractor delay, or audited subsequent penalty recovery would narrow or update the finding; preserve CAG's original period.
limitations: Not a finding of intent, collusion or current 2026 misconduct.
Primary archive publication date not established precisely; observation period is older than most of the requested window.

findings.title: FCI hired CAP storage while owned capacity was vacant
findings.finding: CAG assessed ₹62.76 crore avoidable expenditure associated with 10.55 lakh MT vacant owned CAP capacity alongside hired capacity in Punjab/Haryana.

amount.status: Audit-assessed avoidable expenditure; not foodgrain spoilage

findings.response: FCI management said capacity was hired expecting a bumper paddy crop; cancelling guaranteed-hiring tenders risked litigation. CAG rejected the explanation, citing continued owned-capacity underuse; no Ministry reply was received on this point.
alternativeExplanations: Advance demand uncertainty and guaranteed-hiring contractual commitments, as stated by management.
Seasonal stock movement, suitability and location can make nominal vacant capacity imperfectly substitutable; establish depot-level evidence before extrapolating.
December 2021 CAP phase-out instructions postdate part of the audited decisions and cannot alone establish their intent.
findings.falsifier: Depot-season stock and suitability records, binding contract dates, and documented post-audit action/recoveries could refine the avoidable-cost assessment; no current-status claim without them.
limitations: Audit periods partly predate requested five-year window.
Do not generalize two FCI regions to all India or infer famine risk.
